userStories.title: Make merge-source retirements wait on the replacement (#3052)
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Prevent permanent refusal of a compacted replacement from retiring its source notes, and refuse blank note writes.

**Motivation** — `validateMemoryNoteWrite` (`validate.ts`) checks body size and secrets but not a blank body. A refused merged save currently drains independently from its source forgets, leaving Koda with no replacement and retired sources.

**Approach** — US-001 (nax-agent memory), Target design:

- `MemoryOutboxEntry` and the outbox's `OutboxRequest` (`packages/nax-agent/src/memory/outbox.ts`).
  - Target: both gain `readonly awaits?: string`, the client id of an entry this one must not be delivered before. `EntrySchema` gains `awaits: z.string().regex(MEMORY_CLIENT_ID_RE).optional()`. `enqueue` refuses an `awaits` that does not match `MEMORY_CLIENT_ID_RE` with `MEMORY_CLIENT_ID_INVALID`, before any file is written. `awaits` is queue bookkeeping: `requestOf` (`sync-drain.ts`) never copies it onto the `MemoryWriteRequest` a provider receives.
- `drainOutbox` (`packages/nax-agent/src/memory/sync-drain.ts`).
  - Target: before pushing a queued entry that carries `awaits`, the drain reads the outbox's current state of the awaited id. When the awaited entry is `rejected`, the entry is marked `rejected` without being pushed, with reason `not sent: the replacement it waits on (<awaited slug>) was refused`, and counted in `rejected`. The entry's scope's pull cursor is then rewound with `rewindPullCursor(store, scope)`, as `park` does, so the next pull writes the unsent source back to the mirror (a rejected entry holds no key). When the awaited entry is still `queued`, the entry is not pushed and not counted. When the outbox no longer holds the awaited id, the entry is pushed as before. `proveAndPark` never chooses as its proof an entry whose `awaits` names an entry the outbox still holds.
- `stageAndRecord`, `stageMerge`, `retireMergeSources` (`packages/nax-agent/src/memory/compaction-apply.ts`).
  - Target: each merge's source forgets are enqueued with `awaits` set to the client id of that merge's save (the merged note's id). A plan `retire` is enqueued without `awaits`.
- `validateMemoryNoteWrite` (`packages/nax-agent/src/memory/validate.ts`).
  - Target: a body that holds no non-whitespace character is refused first, with `{ field: "body", reason: "body must not be blank" }`. The size check follows. `validateMemoryCompactionPlan` inherits this through `writeReasons`.

Read-only integration: `applyPushed(input, entry, result)` in memory/delivery.ts; `isMemoryPushRejected(error)` and `isMemoryBadResponse(error)` in memory/note.ts; `MEMORY_CLIENT_ID_RE` and `MEMORY_PUSH_MAX_BAD_RESPONSES` in memory/types.ts. Preserve the existing transient-failure stop and current rollback/archive behavior.

**Interface** — `readonly awaits?: string` on both queue request and entry; `awaits: z.string().regex(MEMORY_CLIENT_ID_RE).optional()` in EntrySchema. Provider-facing `MemoryWriteRequest` is unchanged.

**Scope** — In: outbox persistence and dependency validation, current-state drain gating, proof eligibility, merge save-id hand-off, blank-body validation and cursor rewind. Out: Koda effective proposal-mode refusal belongs to US-006; all tools, chat, sandbox and bot behavior belongs to the other stories. US-001 only: a merge whose save the provider answers as `pending` (a Koda proposal) still delivers its source forgets after it; compaction under Koda proposal mode is refused up front by US-006. US-001 only: compaction undo keeps queuing its removal of a merged note without waiting on the restores it queues. US-001 only: entries queued before this feature carry no `awaits` and drain as before; no migration rewrites them. US-001 only: the local mirror is not rewritten by the drain itself after a refused replacement; the unsent sources come back through the next pull, after the cursor rewind. US-001 only: requeuing a refused save with `outbox.requeue` does not revive the forgets that were rejected while waiting on it; they stay rejected until requeued themselves.

Test implementation: reuse makeMemoryProvider scripted push from packages/nax-agent/test/helpers/memory-provider.ts. Create test/unit/memory/sync-drain-awaits.test.ts for original ACs 5-11, 17-18 and test/integration/memory/compaction-refused-replacement.test.ts for original ACs 1-2, 12-13. Extend outbox.test.ts for ACs 3-4 and validate.test.ts for ACs 14-16. Existing tests hold no awaits entry and do not assert a merge-source forget's full key set. The apply-plus-drain integration must use both public entries with no stub between producer and consumer; retain controls and show new regression cases fail against old code. Setup: project notes budget-a and budget-b, a merge plan over both, and a provider throwing NaxError MEMORY_PUSH_REJECTED for save while answering { id, status: deleted } for forget.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit; spec AC-1] After applyMemoryCompaction merges budget-a and budget-b into budget-a, the queued forget for budget-b carries awaits equal to the clientId of the queued save for budget-a.
[unit; spec AC-2] After applyMemoryCompaction with a plan that retires stale-note, the queued forget for stale-note has no awaits.
[unit; spec AC-3a] outbox.enqueue({ kind: 'forget', …, awaits: 'not a client id!' }) rejects with NaxError code MEMORY_CLIENT_ID_INVALID.
[unit; spec AC-3b] When enqueue refuses the invalid awaits 'not a client id!', outbox.list() stays empty.
[unit; spec AC-4] An entry enqueued with awaits is listed with the same awaits by a second createMemoryOutbox opened over the same directory.
[unit; spec AC-5] When a queued save is permanently refused during drainOutbox and a queued forget awaits it, provider.push never receives the forget.
[unit; spec AC-6] In the refused-save case, the awaiting forget is recorded as { state: 'rejected', reason: 'not sent: the replacement it waits on (budget-a) was refused' }.
[unit; spec AC-7] In the refused-save case, drainOutbox returns pushed: 0 and rejected: 2 (counting the save and the forget), with no failure.
[unit; spec AC-8; control] When the provider accepts the save, provider.push receives the save and then the awaiting forget, in that order, and both entries leave the outbox.
[unit; spec AC-9] A forget whose awaited save the outbox already holds as rejected from an earlier drain is marked rejected by the next drainOutbox without being pushed.
[unit; spec AC-10] A forget whose awaited client id the outbox no longer holds is pushed by drainOutbox.
[unit; spec AC-11a] When an awaited save has met MEMORY_PUSH_MAX_BAD_RESPONSES bad responses and its awaiting forget is the only other queued entry, drainOutbox does not push the forget.
[unit; spec AC-11b] In that bad-response case, outbox.list() still reports the awaited save with state: 'queued', rather than parked as rejected.
[unit; spec AC-11c] In that bad-response case, drainOutbox returns a failure.
[integration; spec AC-12] applyMemoryCompaction merging into budget-a, then drainOutbox with the refusing provider, sends only save:budget-a to provider.push.
[integration; spec AC-13a] applyMemoryCompaction refuses a plan whose merged body is '   ' with MEMORY_COMPACT_PLAN_INVALID.
[integration; spec AC-13b] When applyMemoryCompaction refuses that whitespace-only merged body, the outbox stays empty.
[unit; spec AC-14] validateMemoryNoteWrite with body '  \n\t' (spaces, newline and tab) returns { field: 'body', reason: 'body must not be blank' }.
[unit; spec AC-15] validateMemoryCompactionPlan for a merge into budget-merged with body ' ' returns a reason equal to 'merge target "budget-merged": body must not be blank'.
[unit; spec AC-16; control] validateMemoryNoteWrite with body 'x' and otherwise valid fields returns null.
[unit; spec AC-17] The MemoryWriteRequest provider.push receives for an entry carrying awaits has no awaits key.

[unit; spec AC-18] When drainOutbox marks an awaiting forget rejected because its save was refused, the project scope's pull cursor is rewound, so the next pull call asks the provider with cursor: null.
[failure handling] When a merge's save fails transiently, drainOutbox stops at that save, as today.
[failure handling] When a merge's save fails transiently, its source forgets stay queued for the next sync.

routing.reasoning: Durable queue dependency state spans compaction staging, rejection recovery, proof selection and cursor rewind; real apply-to-drain integration is essential.

userStories.title: Freeze full-network Bash sandbox decisions and disclose the escape (#3053)
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Decide once whether a full-network Bash call runs outside the sandbox and carry that decision through approval and launch.

**Motivation** — Exposure is read again at launch, so a call assessed while unexposed can launch unwrapped with no ask.

**Approach** — US-002 (nax-agent tools), Target design:

- `ToolRunContext` (`packages/nax-agent/src/tools/registry.ts`).
  - Target: gains `readonly fullNetworkUnwrapped?: boolean`: the runtime's one decision about whether a `network: "full"` Bash call runs outside the sandbox.
- `UNSANDBOXED_PREFIX` (`packages/nax-agent/src/tools/ask-request.ts`).
  - Target: exported, unchanged in value. The value is `"; runs OUTSIDE the sandbox: "`.
- A new file `packages/nax-agent/src/tools/runtime-full-network.ts` exports:
  - `fullNetworkUnwrapped(identity: string, input: Record<string, unknown>, port: WebExposurePort | undefined): boolean`. It returns true only when `identity` is `BASH_TOOL_NAME`, `input.network === "full"` and `port?.exposedNetwork?.() !== undefined`.
  - `FULL_NETWORK_UNSANDBOXED_SUFFIX`, built from `UNSANDBOXED_PREFIX` followed by `full network requested`, so it renders `"; runs OUTSIDE the sandbox: full network requested"`.
  - `resolveCallSandbox(p: { identity: string; tool: CodingTool; input: Record<string, unknown>; opts: { readonly unsandboxed?: …; readonly webExposure?: WebExposurePort } }): { readonly call?: UnsandboxedCall; readonly askOption: { readonly unsandboxed?: { readonly suffix: string } }; readonly fullNetworkUnwrapped: boolean }`. It reads `opts.unsandboxed` and `opts.webExposure` itself, so the call site fits on one line. The fields:
    - `call` is exactly what `resolveUnsandboxedCall` answers today, including its `{ kind: "error" }` variant. Only `call` feeds `resolveAskVerdict` and the error return, so the allow-to-ask conversion of an explicit `unsandboxed: true` request (`convertUnsandboxedAllow`) is unchanged.
    - `askOption` is the spread object every ask route receives. It is `{ unsandboxed: { suffix: call.suffix } }` when `call` is the `unsandboxed` variant, else `{ unsandboxed: { suffix: FULL_NETWORK_UNSANDBOXED_SUFFIX } }` when `fullNetworkUnwrapped` is true, else `{}`. A full-network call never becomes an `UnsandboxedCall`, so it is never converted from allow to ask with the "unsandboxed run requested" reason.
- `createCodingToolRuntime(...).callTool` (`packages/nax-agent/src/tools/runtime.ts`).
  - Target: `callTool` calls `resolveCallSandbox({ identity: policyIdentity, tool, input, opts })` once, before the policy check, in place of the `resolveUnsandboxedCall` call. `call` keeps today's error branch and `resolveAskVerdict` input. The policy-ask route's spread becomes `...sandbox.askOption`. The guard-denial route (`resolveWebAwareAskOutcome`) and `resolveWebExposureDenial` also receive `...sandbox.askOption`, and `resolveWebExposureDenial` gains an optional `unsandboxed` parameter it forwards to `resolveAskOutcome`. `runTool` passes `fullNetworkUnwrapped` on the `ToolRunContext`.
  - Line budget: `runtime.ts` must end at 600 lines or fewer (it is 599). The additions above are about +4 lines. To pay for them, the first `resolveWebAwareAskOutcome` route's argument list (the policy-ask route, about 15 lines around line 508) moves into a helper `askThroughGuard(...)` in `runtime-full-network.ts`, which takes the same values and returns that call's promise. `bun run check:file-sizes` passes with the baseline unchanged.
  - A consequence to note: an ask carrying `unsandboxed: true` is never auto-decided (`session-ask-port.ts`), so in a full-mode chat an exposed `network: "full"` Bash call now always waits for a human.
- `requestsUnwrapped` (`packages/nax-agent/src/tools/bash.ts`).
  - Target: `input.unsandboxed === true || (input.network === "full" && (ctx.fullNetworkUnwrapped ?? opts.fullNetwork?.isExposed() === true))`. The context's decision wins when present; a direct call without one keeps today's behaviour.

**Interface** — `readonly fullNetworkUnwrapped?: boolean`; `fullNetworkUnwrapped(identity: string, input: Record<string, unknown>, port: WebExposurePort | undefined): boolean`; `resolveCallSandbox` and `askThroughGuard(...)` as above. Reuse the existing unsandboxed option type represented by the spec's ellipsis, not a new permission mode. Read-only integration: createWebExposureGuard, WebExposureGuard.exposedNetwork(), FULL_NETWORK_REASON text "full network after this session read web content", fullNetworkOption(port), askSummary(tool, scope, input), unsandboxedReasonSuffix, and resolveAskOutcome(p).

**Scope** — In: runtime snapshot, all three ask routes, explicit-unsandboxed compatibility and Bash context hand-off. Out: URL summaries/search/truncation belong to US-003, typed URL origin belongs to US-005, placeholder lifecycle belongs to US-004. US-002 only: `Exec` has no `network` input and is unchanged.

Test implementation: create test/unit/tools/runtime-full-network.test.ts with real createBashTool({ fullNetwork }), a fake launcher capturing unwrapped, an askResolver capturing requests and a controllable webExposure port also used to build fullNetwork. Drive callTool for original ACs 1-7, especially AC 4's unexposed-to-exposed mutation during the policy ask, so the actual runtime-to-Bash context seam is exercised. Extend bash-full-network.test.ts for ACs 8-10. Update integration/web/network-runtime.test.ts's exact ask reason to "full network after this session read web content; runs OUTSIDE the sandbox: full network requested" and assert unsandboxed: true. Retain control cases and strict security TDD isolation.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit; spec AC-1] With the port exposed, createCodingToolRuntime(...).callTool('Bash', { command: 'echo hi', network: 'full' }) raises an ask whose request carries unsandboxed: true.
[unit; spec AC-2] In that exposed full-network case, the request reason equals 'full network after this session read web content; runs OUTSIDE the sandbox: full network requested'.
[unit; spec AC-3] In that case, after the ask is approved, the launcher receives unwrapped: true.

[unit; spec AC-4] When callTool('Bash', { command: 'echo hi', network: 'full' }) starts with an unexposed port and a Bash policy rule answering ask for echo hi, then askResolver exposes the port before approving that policy ask, the approved call launches with unwrapped: false through the real Bash tool.

[unit; spec AC-5] When callTool('Bash', { command: 'echo hi', network: 'full' }) starts exposed and askResolver makes the port unexposed before approving, the approved call launches with unwrapped: true.
[unit; spec AC-6; control] With the port exposed, callTool('Bash', { command: 'echo hi' }) with no network input raises no request carrying unsandboxed: true.
[unit; spec AC-7] fullNetworkUnwrapped('Exec', { network: 'full' }, exposedPort) returns false.
[unit; spec AC-8] Bash.run called directly with { command: 'echo hi', network: 'full' }, fullNetwork.isExposed() false and run context fullNetworkUnwrapped: true launches with unwrapped: true.
[unit; spec AC-9] Bash.run with fullNetwork.isExposed() true and run context fullNetworkUnwrapped: false launches with unwrapped: false.
[unit; spec AC-10; control] Bash.run with fullNetwork.isExposed() true and no fullNetworkUnwrapped in the run context launches with unwrapped: true.
[negative path; refine audit] When an exposed full-network Bash call raises an ask and askResolver denies it, the fake launcher's run method is never called.

routing.reasoning: Security override: sandbox escape approval and session exposure state cross three ask routes and the runtime-to-launch boundary, with assessment/launch races.

modifiedFiles.reason: the assertion that the full-network ask's `reason` is exactly `"full network after this session read web content"` now sees the unsandboxed suffix. The invariant becomes: `reason` equals `"full network after this session read web content; runs OUTSIDE the sandbox: full network requested"`, and the request carries `unsandboxed: true`.

userStories.title: Expose fetch destinations, refuse search redirects and preserve web fences (#3060, #3062, #3063)
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make web approvals identify the destination, reject redirected search responses and retain fenced web trailers under model truncation.

**Motivation** — The search spec (`.nax/features/chat-web-search/spec.md`) requires a non-2xx status to throw `WEB_SEARCH_FAILED`. Fetch asks currently omit their URL and head truncation loses the closing untrusted-content fence.

**Approach** — US-003 (nax-agent web and truncation), Target design:

- `fetchTool` (`packages/nax-agent/src/web/provider.ts`).
  - Target: the provider tool declares `summaryFields: ["url"]`.
- `send` (`packages/nax-agent/src/web/search-request.ts`).
  - Target: `_webSearchDeps.fetch(request.url, { ...request.init, redirect: "manual", signal })`. A 3xx then reaches `assertStatus` and throws `WEB_SEARCH_FAILED` with message `<backend> search failed with status <status>` and context `{ backend, status }`.
- `packages/nax-agent/src/web/content.ts` exports `WEB_CONTENT_CLOSE_LINE = "</web-content>"`, and `fenceWebContent` uses it. `content.ts` keeps importing nothing, so `tools/spill.ts` may import it without a cycle.
- `composeHead` / `applyModelTruncationPolicy` (`packages/nax-agent/src/tools/spill.ts`).
  - Target: when the head direction truncates a body whose first line starts with `<web-content ` and which has a **web trailer**, the result ends with the marker line followed by that trailer. The trailer is the last line equal to `WEB_CONTENT_CLOSE_LINE` plus every line after it, provided at most one line follows it (the fetch tool's `[truncated at <n> bytes]` line). The trailer is taken from the original `body`, before `truncateForModel` runs, because `shaped.content` has already lost it. Its bytes and lines are reserved from the same byte cap and `MODEL_MAX_LINES` before the head is cut. Every other body is shaped exactly as today.

**Interface** — `summaryFields: ["url"]`; `WEB_CONTENT_CLOSE_LINE = "</web-content>"`; `_webSearchDeps.fetch(request.url, { ...request.init, redirect: "manual", signal })`. Read-only integration: askSummary(tool, scope, input); MODEL_MAX_BYTES (40,000), MODEL_MAX_LINES (1,000), truncationDirectionFor and splitModelLines from tools/truncate.ts; fenceWebContent({ source, fetchedAt, text }) output starts with `<web-content source="…" fetched="…" untrusted="true">`, then newline, text, newline and `</web-content>`. Preserve shared byte/line cap behavior and existing spill handling.

**Scope** — In: provider summary metadata through adaptation and runtime asks, shared search transport redirect policy, closing-line constant and original-body trailer-aware head composition. Out: full-network approval/launch decisions belong to US-002, typed seen-URL recording belongs to US-005. US-003 only: a truncated web result is not re-fetchable by offset; the spill file remains the only copy of the cut text. US-003 only: tail-direction truncation (Bash and other command tools) is unchanged.

Test implementation: extend existing adapted-provider askSummary tests and exposed-session runtime coverage to assert the exact URL-bearing summary. Extend unit/web/search-backend-exa-searxng.test.ts's SearXNG fetch stub for 302 and capture every backend's redirect init; no existing search test answers a 3xx. Create test/unit/tools/spill-web-fence.test.ts for original ACs 6-11 using real fenceWebContent, including 1,103 lines, a 200 KB paragraph at maxBytes 4000, an existing fetch byte-truncation suffix and the non-web <project> control. No existing test fences a web result past the caps. Strict TDD applies because approval visibility and untrusted-content isolation are security-sensitive.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit; spec AC-1] askSummary('web__fetch', scope, { url: 'https://docs.example.com/guide' }), with the scope of the adapted fetch tool from createWebToolProvider, returns summary 'web__fetch url=https://docs.example.com/guide'.
[integration; spec AC-2] In an exposed session, callTool('web__fetch', { url: 'https://unseen.example/page' }) raises an ask whose summary equals 'web__fetch url=https://unseen.example/page'.
[unit; spec AC-3] A SearXNG search whose _webSearchDeps.fetch stub answers status 302 with a location header rejects with NaxError code WEB_SEARCH_FAILED and context status: 302.
[unit; spec AC-4] In that SearXNG 302 case, the rejection message equals 'searxng search failed with status 302'.
[unit; spec AC-5] Every backend's request reaches _webSearchDeps.fetch with redirect: 'manual' in its init.
[unit; spec AC-6] applyModelTruncationPolicy over fenceWebContent of a 1,103-line text, with toolName: 'web__fetch', returns a result whose last line is '</web-content>'.
[unit; spec AC-7] In that 1,103-line fenced case, the result has at most MODEL_MAX_LINES lines.
[unit; spec AC-8] In that 1,103-line fenced case, the line before '</web-content>' is the truncation marker, which starts with '... [truncated'.
[unit; spec AC-9a] With maxBytes: 4000 and a fenced 200 KB single-paragraph text, applyModelTruncationPolicy returns a result whose UTF-8 byte length is at most 4000.
[unit; spec AC-9b] With maxBytes: 4000 and a fenced 200 KB single-paragraph text, the result's last line is '</web-content>'.
[unit; spec AC-10] When a fenced body followed by a '[truncated at 2000000 bytes]' line is cut by the policy, its last two lines are '</web-content>' and then '[truncated at 2000000 bytes]'.
[unit; spec AC-11; control] A body whose first line is '<project>' and whose last line is '</project>', cut by the head direction, ends with the truncation marker as its last line.

routing.reasoning: Four bounded source edits reuse provider metadata, search status handling and existing truncation composition; strict three-session TDD remains required for approval disclosure and the untrusted web-content boundary.

userStories.title: Abandon stale placeholder candidates and preserve platform/file-mode semantics (#3055, #3059, #3061)
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Stop pending placeholder candidates from adopting later user files, limit mandatory staging exclusions to Linux and preserve exclude-file permissions.

**Motivation** — A user file created later at that path, empty and placeholder-shaped, is adopted by the next `observe`.

**Approach** — US-004 (nax-agent sandbox), Target design:

- `stagingPlaceholderPaths(cwd, trackedPaths)` (`packages/nax-agent/src/sandbox/staging-placeholders.ts`).
  - Target: the `SRT_MANDATORY_DENY_FILES` / `SRT_MANDATORY_DENY_DIRS` sources are used only when `_placeholderDeps.platform()` is `"linux"`. The ledger entries are used on every platform, as today (a ledger exists only on Linux).
- `replaceAtomically(path, content, mode)` (`packages/nax-agent/src/sandbox/placeholder-excludes.ts`).
  - Target: when `mode` is defined, the temp file is `chmod`ed to `mode` after it is written and before the rename, so the result carries the original permission bits regardless of the umask.
- `PlaceholderLedger.prune` (`packages/nax-agent/src/sandbox/placeholder-ledger.ts`).
  - Target: `prune(opts?: { readonly abandonPending?: boolean }): void`. With `abandonPending: true` the pending entries are dropped too. Without the option, behaviour is unchanged.
- The srt backend (`packages/nax-agent/src/sandbox/srt-backend.ts`).
  - Target: it counts wraps in flight. The count goes up where `recordPlaceholderCandidates` runs for a wrap. It goes down in `commandFinished`, and also when `wrapWithSandboxArgv` throws after the candidates were recorded, because a failed wrap is never followed by `commandFinished`. It never goes below 0. `commandFinished` calls `prune({ abandonPending: true })` when that count reaches 0, and `prune()` otherwise. `reset()` calls `prune({ abandonPending: true })` and sets the count to 0.

**Interface** — `prune(opts?: { readonly abandonPending?: boolean }): void`; `stagingPlaceholderPaths(cwd, trackedPaths)` and `replaceAtomically(path, content, mode)` keep their existing call contracts. Read-only integration: `_placeholderDeps.platform()`, `_placeholderDeps.ledgerDir()` and `placeholderIdentity(path)`. Do not replace trusted identity matching with shape-only deletion.

**Scope** — In: pending-ledger abandon points including wrap failure/reset, concurrent wrap count, Linux-only mandatory-name staging sources and temp-file chmod. Out: approval and Bash wrapping decisions belong to US-002; unrelated web, chat, memory and bot changes belong to their own stories. US-004 only: ledgers already written by earlier versions are not rewritten; their pending entries are dropped at the next abandon point of this process or by the existing sweep.

Test implementation: extend unit/sandbox/staging-placeholders.test.ts, unit/sandbox/placeholder-excludes.test.ts and unit/sandbox/placeholder-ledger.test.ts; create unit/sandbox/srt-backend-ledger-abandon.test.ts for original ACs 8-12. Use the existing ledger fixtures over _placeholderDeps, real temp paths, controlled wraps and reset singleton/deps state. Restore process.umask after permission assertions. Add the darwin gitlinkSafeAdd integration case. Existing Linux-placeholder expectations must explicitly set _placeholderDeps.platform = () => "linux" in unit/sandbox/staging-placeholders.test.ts, unit/internal/git-add.test.ts's "with a placeholder in the tree (US-006)" describe, integration/sandbox/staging-placeholders-git-add.test.ts, unit/tools/git-commit.test.ts's "gitCommitTool — a placeholder is never committed (US-006)" describe, and unit/sandbox/policy-builder-root-denies.test.ts. In unit/sandbox/srt-backend.test.ts, "US-003 AC5: a .bashrc the user wrote before the first wrap never enters the ledger" must keep .bashrc out of the ledger and assert .zprofile while a wrap is in flight, before the last commandFinished; it is no longer pending afterwards. Preserve observe-before-cleanup identity capture, no-option prune controls and all trust checks. Show regressions fail against old code under strict security TDD.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit; spec AC-1] With _placeholderDeps.platform answering 'darwin', stagingPlaceholderPaths(cwd, []) over a directory holding an empty mode-0444 .mcp.json returns [].
[unit; spec AC-2; control] With _placeholderDeps.platform answering 'linux', stagingPlaceholderPaths(cwd, []) over the same empty mode-0444 .mcp.json returns ['.mcp.json'].

[integration; spec AC-3a] With _placeholderDeps.platform answering 'darwin', gitlinkSafeAdd over a fresh repository holding an untracked empty mode-0444 .mcp.json adds .mcp.json to the index, as observed through git diff --cached --name-only.
[integration; spec AC-3b] In that darwin gitlinkSafeAdd case, git ls-files lists .mcp.json.
[unit; spec AC-4] Under process.umask(0o022), ensurePlaceholderExcludes(cwd) over a repository whose .git/info/exclude has mode 0664 leaves the file at mode 0664.
[unit; spec AC-5; control] In that exclude-file case, the exclude file ends with every PLACEHOLDER_EXCLUDE_ENTRIES line.
[unit; spec AC-6] A ledger that called recordAbsent for one path, then prune({ abandonPending: true }), leaves no ledger file on disk.
[unit; spec AC-7; control] A ledger that called recordAbsent for one path, then prune(), still lists that path as a pending entry in readLedgerFile.
[unit; spec AC-8] With two wraps in flight, the first commandFinished leaves the pending entry in the ledger file.
[unit; spec AC-9] In that two-wrap case, the second commandFinished removes the pending entry from the ledger file.

[unit; spec AC-10] After the last commandFinished abandons a pending path and a user creates an empty mode-0444 file there, a later placeholderLedger().observe() with no new wrap leaves no ledger file in the ledger directory listing that path.
[unit; spec AC-11; failure handling] reset() with one wrap in flight removes that wrap's pending entries from the ledger file, including a candidate whose wrap never finishes.
[unit; spec AC-12] When one wrap's wrapWithSandboxArgv throws and another wrap then runs to its commandFinished, that commandFinished removes the pending entries from the ledger file.

routing.reasoning: Security override: trusted sandbox placeholder ownership and cleanup interact with concurrent wrap lifecycles, platform-specific staging and file permissions.

userStories.title: Record seen URLs only from typed sends and accepted human steers (#3054)
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Move seen-URL recording to human input at the chat host and carry automatic origin through generated notices.

**Motivation** — A model-authored background command can therefore mark any URL as seen, and a later `web__fetch` of that URL skips the unseen-URL ask.

**Approach** — US-005 (nax chat), Target design:

- `ChatSendOptions` (`packages/nax/src/chat/chat-host-types.ts`).
  - Target: gains `readonly automatic?: boolean`: a host-generated turn (a background-task or job notice), whose text is never recorded as seen URLs.
- `ChatHost.steer` (`chat-host-types.ts`, `chat-host.ts`, `createHostSteering` in `host-steer-compact.ts`).
  - Target: `steer?(text: string, options?: { readonly automatic?: boolean }): SteerResult`. When the session answers `accepted` and `options?.automatic !== true`, the URLs in the typed text are recorded on the open handle's web exposure. `HostSteerInput` gains `readonly web: () => ChatWeb | undefined`, which `NativeChatHost` supplies from its open handle, and `createHostSteering` does the recording, so `chat-host.ts` only forwards `options`. A typed steer is called with one argument (`steer(text)`), never with an explicit `undefined` second argument.
- A new export `recordTypedUrls(web: ChatWeb | undefined, message: string): void` in `packages/nax/src/chat/session-web.ts` holds the one recording rule: `web.exposure.recordUrls(extractWebUrls(parseMentionMessage(message)?.text ?? message))`, and nothing when `web` is undefined.
- `wrapWebSession` (`session-web.ts`).
  - Target: `send` no longer records. It keeps its drain-around-events behaviour.
- `NativeChatHost.send` (`packages/nax/src/chat/chat-host.ts`).
  - Target: when `options?.automatic !== true`, it calls `recordTypedUrls(this.handle.web, message)` synchronously, after the `CHAT_TURN_BUSY` rejection (a rejected send records nothing) and before the turn's `handle.session.send` is called. `chat-host.ts` stays at 600 lines or fewer.
- `ChatApp` job and task notice delivery (`packages/nax/src/tui/chat/ChatApp.tsx`, `use-jobs.ts`).
  - Target: `ComposedSend` gains `readonly automatic?: boolean`. `deliver` passes `sendTurn({ message: text, automatic: true })`. `sendMessage` adds `automatic: true` to the options it passes `host.send` exactly when the composed send carries it, so a notice reaches `host.send(text, onEvent, { automatic: true })` with no `title`. A steered notice calls `host.steer(notice, { automatic: true })`. A typed message and a typed steer are unchanged: no `automatic`.

**Interface** — `readonly automatic?: boolean` on ChatSendOptions and ComposedSend; `steer?(text: string, options?: { readonly automatic?: boolean }): SteerResult`; `readonly web: () => ChatWeb | undefined` on HostSteerInput; `recordTypedUrls(web: ChatWeb | undefined, message: string): void`. Read-only integration: parseMentionMessage(message) in chat/mentions/mention-envelope.ts, extractWebUrls(text) from @nathapp/nax-agent/internal, and buildBackgroundTaskNotice in prompts/builders/background-builder.ts.

**Scope** — In: synchronous host-send recording, accepted human steer recording, mention-envelope text-only extraction, generated notice origin through idle and busy TUI routes, and wrapper drain preservation. Out: full-network escape handling belongs to US-002, fetch summary/search/fence behavior belongs to US-003. US-005 only: URLs pasted into a slash command's arguments are recorded exactly as a typed message is today.

Test implementation: create test/unit/chat/chat-host-web-urls.test.ts with a NativeChatHost over the web-enabled native handle fixture and a scripted session.send, as open-chat-session-web.test.ts builds it. The old open-chat-session-web.test.ts AC-9 must now assert handle.session.send alone records nothing and still forwards message and input unchanged; the synchronous typed-URL assertion moves to ChatHost.send. Its AC-10 attachment case must drive ChatHost.send with the same empty seenUrls expectation. Extend test/ui/chat/task-notices.test.tsx's mounted ChatApp helper, entering from background-task completion and asserting exact host.send options { automatic: true } when idle, host.steer(notice, { automatic: true }) when busy, and unchanged typed-message behavior. Exercise actual option producers and host consumers, not only recordTypedUrls in isolation. Strict TDD applies to this session URL-approval trust boundary.

[integration; spec AC-7] In a mounted ChatApp with no turn running, a background task that ends delivers its notice through host.send with options exactly { automatic: true }.

userStories.title: Refuse compaction under Koda's effective proposal mode (#3056)
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make compaction apply and undo honor the provider's current effective Koda write policy before any operation runs. **Motivation** — Koda decides the effective mode per principal (`proposal` for an agent under an approval policy), and the Koda provider already reads `GET projects/

/memory/write-mode` in `reachable()` (`koda-provider.ts`). **Approach** — US-006 (nax memory), Target design: - `createKodaMemoryProvider` (`packages/nax/src/memory/koda-provider.ts`). - Target: returns `KodaMemoryProvider = MemoryProvider & { effectiveWriteMode(): Promise<"direct" | "proposal"> }`. `effectiveWriteMode` reads `GET projects//memory/write-mode` on every call, with no memo, because a policy change on Koda must be seen. It resolves `data.mode` when it is `direct` or `proposal`. Otherwise it throws `NaxError` `MEMORY_KODA_BAD_RESPONSE`, and a client failure propagates unchanged. - A new export `effectiveWriteModeOf(provider: MemoryProvider): (() => Promise<"direct" | "proposal">) | undefined` in `koda-provider.ts` answers the method when the provider has one. - `HostCompactionInput` and `createHostCompaction` (`packages/nax/src/memory/host-compact.ts`). - Target: `providerId: string` is replaced by `provider: MemoryProvider`, and the manifest's provider label reads `provider.id`. Apply and undo refuse with `MEMORY_COMPACT_UNSUPPORTED` when the local `writeMode` is `proposal`, or when `effectiveWriteModeOf(input.provider)` exists and resolves `proposal`. A rejected lookup propagates, and no operation is called. `createMemoryHost` (`host.ts`) passes `provider: parts.provider` in place of `providerId: parts.provider.id`, so `host.ts` does not grow. **Interface** — `KodaMemoryProvider = MemoryProvider & { effectiveWriteMode(): Promise<"direct" | "proposal"> }`; `effectiveWriteModeOf(provider: MemoryProvider): (() => Promise<"direct" | "proposal">) | undefined`; HostCompactionInput receives `provider: MemoryProvider` instead of `providerId: string`. Keep generic/local MemoryProvider compatibility and reachable()'s boolean probe behavior; no effective-mode memoization. **Scope** — In: fresh Koda write-mode capability, validated response/error propagation, local-or-effective proposal refusal for apply/undo, provider hand-off and unchanged string provider label in compaction operations. Out: outbox merge dependencies and blank-write validation belong to US-001; chat, web tools, sandbox and bot fixes belong to their own stories. Proposal-mode compaction itself remains unsupported; this story refuses it rather than building an approval workflow. Test implementation: extend test/unit/memory/koda-provider-save.test.ts using its scripted Koda client for proposal, two fresh requests and malformed responses. Create test/unit/memory/host-compact-koda-mode.test.ts for original ACs 4-9 with operations spies and local-provider controls. For AC 9, construct createMemoryHost configured for memory.provider: koda with a Koda client stub and invoke the returned host.applyCompaction, exercising host.ts's provider hand-off rather than bypassing it. host.ts exposes the composed applyCompaction method directly; there is no nested host.compaction property. Existing test/integration/memory/host-compaction.test.ts builds a local provider through createMemoryHost; its operation provider label remains that provider's id and no test currently constructs HostCompactionInput by hand. Include both apply and undo lookup-failure cases from Failure Handling: propagate the identical error with no operation and no staging. Preserve host.ts's 600-line budget by replacing the argument, not adding logic there. Strict TDD applies because the effective mode is an access-policy decision.

userStories.title: Preserve staged ledger edits and carry divergent audit entries (#3057, #3058)
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Commit advisor ledger appends without clearing a different user-staged version and carry complete missing main-ledger lines into divergent PR ledgers.

**Motivation** — That clears a different ledger version the user staged during the run. The divergent PR ledger also misses main's newer audit entries.

**Approach** — US-007 (nax bot), Target design:

- `commitExactText` / `refreshIndexEntry` (`packages/nax/src/bot/ledger-carry.ts`).
  - Target: `refreshIndexEntry` receives the parent commit's blob for `rel`, looked up in `commitExactText` with `git rev-parse <parent>:<rel>` (a failure means the file was absent), and the new commit's `blob`. After `update-ref`, it reads the user's current index entry blob for `rel` (`git ls-files -s -- :(literal)<rel>` against the real index). It resets the entry to HEAD only when that blob equals the parent's blob or the new commit's blob, or when the entry and the parent's blob are both absent. Otherwise it leaves the index alone and warns `Advisor ledger committed; the staged ledger differs and was left as is`. When the index read fails, it skips the reset with the same warn.
- `carry` (`ledger-carry.ts`).
  - Target: a new exported `mergedLedgerText(previous: string | null, main: string): string | null`.
    - It answers `main` when `isLedgerAppend(previous, main)` holds, `previous` is `null`, empty or ends in a newline, and `main` ends in a newline. A character-level append onto an unterminated last line, or one that ends in an unterminated line, goes to the line merge below instead.
    - Otherwise it answers `previous`, with a newline added when it lacks a trailing one, followed by every **complete** line of `main` that `previous` does not hold, in main's order, each ending in a newline. A complete line is a non-empty line followed by a newline, so an unterminated last line of `main` is never carried.
    - "`previous` holds a line" means the line equals one of previous's lines, its unterminated last line included. A line repeated in `main` is carried once. `previous = null` is an empty prefix.
    - It answers `null` when no complete line is missing.
  - `carry` commits that text with the existing add-and-commit path. `null` always means no carry: `carry` warns "Main checkout ledger does not extend the PR's; not carried" and returns false with no commit. This includes `previous = "a\n"` with `main = "a\nb"`, which today commits `"a\nb"` and now waits until main's last line is complete. The PR's own lines are never reordered or removed.

**Interface** — `mergedLedgerText(previous: string | null, main: string): string | null`. Extend refreshIndexEntry's existing inputs with parent blob and new blob; use the real index for the post-update-ref inspection, not the throwaway index used to construct the commit. Read-only integration: ledgerPath(repoRoot, feature) in advisor/ledger.ts. Keep isLedgerAppend's exported contract for its other consumer, private-copy hashing, signing, CAS update-ref, add-and-commit rollback and worktree isolation unchanged. The explicit ACs place the current-index read after update-ref; unreadable index must not undo or fail a committed append.

**Scope** — In: parent/current/new blob comparison, successful-commit behavior on index-read failure, complete-line merge and divergent PR carry. Out: placeholder-related staging changes belong to US-004; memory, chat and web fixes belong to their own stories. US-007 only: a PR ledger line that the main ledger also holds, at a different position, is not moved.

Test implementation: no new files. Extend test/unit/bot/ledger-carry.test.ts, test/integration/bot/ledger-in-place.test.ts and test/integration/bot/ledger-carry.test.ts. The unit "AC-5–8: %s main ledger is not carried" grouping currently includes equal, missing, divergent and shorter; divergent (main "other\nnew\n" against PR "old\n") now carries "old\nother\nnew\n" with no warn, while equal/missing/shorter retain their expectations and shorter main "ol" still skips with the same warn. For the index race, wrap _ledgerCarryDeps.runGit to git add a different ledger version just before update-ref and assert through real git ls-files -s that it survives while HEAD contains the appended text. Include the unchanged-index control and index-read failure after a successful commit. Drive divergent carry with separate main and PR worktrees; do not replace the real repository seam with only text-helper unit tests. Show noncontrol regressions fail against old code and preserve the existing tests for concurrent working-file edits and unrelated staged files.

analysis:
This is a bounded corrective enhancement to existing TypeScript code, closing #3052, #3053, #3054, #3055, #3056, #3057, #3058, #3059, #3060, #3061, #3062 and #3063. Preserve exactly seven independent implementation stories, with no dependencies: US-001 through US-004 are wholly in packages/nax-agent; US-005 through US-007 are wholly in packages/nax. No nax-ai or nax-agent-acp implementation changes are needed. Graph navigation was unavailable in this host, so findings below were obtained by direct reads and targeted text searches, not an indexed graph. The external review report was not available and was not independently inspected.

Architecture and constraints: docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:145 documents the 600-line hard source cap and 400-line soft limit; the spec specifically requires runtime.ts (currently 599 lines), chat-host.ts (595), and memory/host.ts (600) to remain within 600 without changing the baseline. Put runtime helper logic in runtime-full-network.ts, chat steering recording in host-steer-compact.ts and URL parsing in session-web.ts; replace the memory host provider argument without growing host.ts. ChatApp.tsx is exempt from this cap. nax-agent is a Node-compatible ESM library: use Node APIs, runtimeSpawn/getAgentRuntime rather than direct child_process/Bun spawn, #src imports, explicit .ts extensions on relative source imports, and exported _deps seams for external calls (packages/nax-agent/AGENTS.md:117). nax is Bun-native with React TUI and its own @/ aliases (packages/nax/AGENTS.md:21). Keep package boundaries, dependency direction and named public exports. Internal-only helper exports do not imply root public API additions; inspect whether changed public declarations require the normal nax-agent API snapshot update, rather than exporting implementation helpers from the public entry. All package commands run from their package directory; never bare bun test. Regression tests must demonstrate failure against the old implementation, with the spec's control cases retained. Existing fixtures should be extended rather than duplicated. No source changes or tests were run during PRD drafting.

US-001 findings: packages/nax-agent/src/memory/outbox.ts:59 defines OutboxRequest without dependencies, :62 defines MemoryOutboxEntry, :117 defines the durable EntrySchema, and :291 prepares ids before writes. withClientId/writeEntry currently type the prepared request as MemoryWriteRequest; propagate the new queue-only awaits field through the enqueue preparation and persistence types so it is neither erased on reload nor accidentally forwarded to a provider. The outbox writes one atomic JSON entry per request; rejected records remain and heldKeys includes only queued records (outbox.ts:378). packages/nax-agent/src/memory/sync-drain.ts:55 already projects a provider request explicitly; preserve that projection to keep awaits private. drainOutbox at :182 snapshots queued entries, settle at :138 removes delivered entries or preserves permanent rejections, and proveAndPark at :225 currently chooses any later different-key entry. Dependency checks must use the CURRENT outbox, not the original queue snapshot, so a save refused earlier in the same drain blocks its forgets, a save accepted and removed releases them, and a prior rejected save is also respected. Exclude blocked dependents from bad-response proof selection or a forget can delete a source while being used to justify parking its replacement. park at :253 already demonstrates the cursor rewind needed when an unsent dependent is rejected. packages/nax-agent/src/memory/compaction-apply.ts:276 stages saves, standalone retires and source forgets separately; stageMerge at :357 mints the note id and enqueues save with that clientId, while retireMergeSources at :407 currently passes no relationship. Retain each merge's save id across those phases without changing rollback tracking, archives, locking, manifest contents or standalone retire behavior. validate.ts:74 checks only body size, and validateMemoryNoteWrite at :118 composes validation in order; blank-body validation must precede body size and flow through compaction plan writeReasons. Consumers include memory/sync.ts:64, memory/index.ts:1 and internal.ts:51. Reuse test/helpers/memory-provider.ts:97's scripted push/pull mocks and existing unit/memory/outbox.test.ts, validate.test.ts and compaction-apply-staged-writes.test.ts. Add the specified unit drain and public apply-plus-drain integration files; do not stub the producer/consumer seam. Migration is additive: optional awaits means old entry files remain readable and drain unchanged; no backfill, revival or undo dependency rewrite. Rejected source notes reappear through the next pull after rewind, not an immediate mirror rewrite.

US-002 findings: packages/nax-agent/src/tools/runtime.ts:385 resolves only explicit unsandboxed requests before policy.check. Its runTool closure at :432 builds ToolRunContext; the policy ask at :507, command-guard ask at :558 and exposure-only ask at :579 must all receive the same sandbox.askOption. runtime-web-guard.ts:76's exposure-only route currently has no unsandboxed parameter, whereas resolveWebAwareAskOutcome at :130 already passes through resolveAskOutcome parameters. runtime-calltool.ts:217 handles explicit escape enablement and error variants; convertUnsandboxedAllow at :254 is deliberately separate from ordinary full-network exposure asks and must remain unchanged. ask-request.ts:89 holds the exact private suffix prefix to export. Explicit input.unsandboxed === true remains authoritative. The runtime helper should depend on runtime-calltool/runtime-web-guard and use type-only runtime references where needed to avoid an initialization cycle. session/session-ask-port.ts:54 forwards unsandboxed asks as never auto-decided, so exposed full-network commands now wait for humans even in full-mode chats. This is an intended approval change, not a policy-mode rewrite. Existing unit/tools/bash-full-network.test.ts:30 captures launcher.unwrapped; integration/web/network-runtime.test.ts:103 asserts the old exact reason and must assert the new suffix and flag. Reserve trailer separators, bytes and lines alongside marker budgeting; respect UTF-8 byte cutting and the 1,000-line limit while preserving the optional fetch byte-cap line. Do not generalize closing-fence handling to arbitrary XML or change command-tail composition at spill.ts:205. Both runtime.ts:319 and the native after_tool policy use this shared shaping surface; regressions must preserve non-web and nontruncated behavior, spill recovery and existing marker semantics. Extend search-backend-exa-searxng.test.ts and existing provider/runtime coverage, plus the specified spill-web-fence test file.
